name: Shorecrest

stage_evidence.note: Described as currently under construction in reporting of 21 August 2026

name: Banyan Tree Residences West Palm Beach
description: 25-storey residential development with 88 condominium residences, interiors by Yabu Pushelberg and landscape architecture by Enea Landscape Architecture. One block from CityPlace and two from the Intracoastal Waterway. Unanimously approved by the Downtown Action Committee in August 2026.
notes: OMA (Jason Long) is the design architect and Corwil Architects is the architect of record, so Corwil is stored and OMA recorded here, per the field rule. The storey count was published as 24 and 28 in March 2026 and as 25 in August 2026; the later figure is stored. The project is reported at 400 Hibiscus Street and at 635 South Dixie Highway with the same 88-residence, Mast Capital/Curated JCZM programme, which is one corner site under two frontages.

stage_evidence.note: Podium construction continuing with tower crane in place, reported 3 August 2026

description: 27-storey mixed-use tower in Downtown West Palm Beach yielding 110 hotel suites and 146 branded residences, with interiors by Meyer Davis. Broke ground in 2025.

name: Alba Palm Beach

stage_evidence.note: Photographs of the completed tower, residences and amenity spaces published 22 June 2026; the Palm Beach County parcel record for 4714 N Flagler Dr now carries individual condominium units conveyed to separate owners, which is the closing of sales

description: 22-storey waterfront condominium on the Intracoastal Waterway in the Northwood neighbourhood with 55 residences. Topped off May 2025; both tower cranes removed by July 2025.
notes: Completion rests on two things rather than a certificate of occupancy: the June 2026 report of the finished building, and the county parcel record, which now holds separate per-unit parcel control numbers with individual owners at this address. The City of West Palm Beach permit portal is a session-driven application that refused automated requests, so no certificate of occupancy was read directly.

name: 120 South Dixie Highway
description: 25-storey mixed-income tower of 399 apartments, about 160 of them for households at or below 120 per cent of area median income, with roughly 7,550 sq ft of retail and 236 parking spaces. Studio to three-bedroom units of 505 to 1,320 sq ft; workforce units on floors two to four and six to eleven, market-rate above. A prefabricated mass timber system would make it the tallest wood-framed building in Florida. Incorporates an abandoned fire station into the main floor.
notes: Unit count conflict settled: 399 units, stated by Florida YIMBY and The Real Deal in May 2026. A 366-unit figure circulated earlier and is superseded. Nexus Systems is named on the development team for the mass timber system.

name: 2085 North Flagler Drive
description: Two 31-storey towers requiring close to 440,000 sq ft of new construction on a 1.55-acre site.
notes: The site was under contract from its owner, 2111 Flagler LLC, at the time of reporting. No unit count or architect is published.

name: The Ritz-Carlton Residences, West Palm Beach
description: 27-storey waterfront condominium tower in the North Flagler District, developed in partnership with Marriott International, with interiors by Rockwell Group and landscape design by Naturalficial. 138 residences averaging approximately 2,500 sq ft.
notes: Storey count published as 26 in October 2025 and 27 in February 2026; the later figure is stored. The 138-residence figure comes from a multi-project round-up where attribution is by paragraph, so it is less firmly attributed than the rest of this record. A $600m Bank OZK construction loan reported in the same round-up is attributed in its own headline to South Flagler House, not to this project, so no lender is recorded here.

name: The Mandarin Oriental Residences, West Palm Beach
description: 31-storey luxury condominium tower on the Intracoastal Waterway with 87 residences priced from approximately $3.5m, on a 2.46-acre site in Pinewood Park bounded by the Intracoastal to the east and 54th Street to the north, replacing a 72-unit low-rise completed in 1966. Approved by the West Palm Beach Planning Board in August 2025. Groundbreaking estimated 2027, completion 2029 to 2031.
notes: Unit count published as 97 residences in August 2025 and 87 in March and May 2026; the later figure is stored. Safdie Architects and Spina O'Rourke + Partners are both named on the architecture and the sources do not say which is architect of record; Safdie is stored and Spina O'Rourke recorded here.
